questions.question: If a cylinder with radius (R) and Length (L) is given, give the expression to find out the twisting couple of the cylinder / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• If a cylinder with radius (R) and length (L) is given, give the expression to find out
  • the twisting couple of the cylinder.
  • Answer:
  • Twisting couple, C = (π η R⁴ θ) / (2L). (1 mark)
  • η – rigidity modulus, R – radius, L – length, θ – angle of twist. (1 mark)
  • [A] / [CO2]

questions.question: Explain about the different elastic behavior of solids. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain about the different elastic behavior of solids.
  • Answer:
  • Solids obey Hooke’s law for small deformations. (1 mark)
  • Beyond the elastic limit, permanent deformation starts. (1 mark)
  • Ductile materials show large plastic strain before breaking. (1 mark)
  • Brittle materials break without much deformation. (1 mark)
  • Area under stress–strain curve shows resilience and toughness. (1 mark)
  • [U] / [CO1]

questions.question: How can we compare moments of inertia using torsion pendulum? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• How can we compare moments of inertia using torsion pendulum?
  • Answer:
  • Time period T = 2π√(I/C). (1 mark)
  • Measure time period of platform alone (T₀) and with the body (T). (1 mark)
  • Moment of inertia of body, I = (C/4π²)(T² – T₀²). (1 mark)
  • For two bodies, I₁/I₂ = (T₁² – T₀²)/(T₂² – T₀²). (1 mark)
  • Hence moments of inertia can be compared experimentally. (1 mark)
  • [K] / [CO2]

questions.question: Calculate the Reynold’s number for water flowing through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m at avelocity 2 m/s. Given density of water=1000 kg/m3 and viscosity of water=0.001 Pa.s / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Calculate the Reynold’s number for water flowing through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m
  • at a velocity 2 m/s. Given density = 1000 kg/m³ and viscosity = 0.001 Pa·s.
  • Answer:
  • Formula: Re = (ρ v D) / μ. (1 mark)
  • Substitute: Re = (1000 × 2 × 0.1) / 0.001. (1 mark)
  • Re = 2 × 10⁵. (1 mark)
  • Re > 4000, so the flow is turbulent. (1 mark)
  • Reynolds number is dimensionless. (1 mark)
  • [A] / [CO3]

questions.question: Calculate the velocity with which a source of frequency 10000 Hz should approach an observer at rest in order to produce a Doppler shift of 200 Hz. Velocity of sound 332m/s. / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Calculate the velocity with which a source of frequency 10000 Hz should approach
  • an observer at rest in order to produce a Doppler shift of 200 Hz. Velocity of sound =
  • 332 m/s.
  • Answer:
  • Given f = 10000 Hz, f′ = 10200 Hz, v = 332 m/s. (1 mark)
  • Formula: f′ = f × [v / (v – vₛ)]. (1 mark)
  • 10200/10000 = 332 / (332 – vₛ). (1 mark)
  • vₛ = 6.5 m/s. (1 mark)
  • Hence, the source must approach at about 6.5 m/s. (1 mark)
  • [U] / [CO6]

  • Answer:
  • Mach number M = V / a (speed / speed of sound). (1 mark)
  • M < 1: subsonic, M = 1: sonic, M > 1: supersonic. (1 mark)
  • Compressibility effects increase with M. (1 mark)
  • Shock waves form when M ≥ 1. (1 mark)
  • Mach number helps classify aircraft speed and design. (1 mark)
